channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Nicotine Pouches Are Not Cigarettes. Regulation Should Reflect the Difference
item.description: A nicotine pouch is not a cigarette without smoke; it is a different product category altogether. That distinction matters for regulation, because rules designed around combustion do not automatically make sense for oral, smoke-free nicotine. Pouches still need standards, age controls and monitoring, but policy should reflect their actual risk profile rather than the stigma attached to cigarettes. Regulation is most credible when it recognises differences instead of flattening them. (Published on August 03, 2026byvapingpost.com)

item.title: Two Presentations, One Crisis: When the Evidence Points Beyond Enforcement
item.description: Two presentations can reveal one crisis when the same evidence points are interpreted in opposite ways. In nicotine policy, that crisis is not only about disagreement — it is about whether science is being used to clarify risk or to defend existing positions. When data on safer products is filtered through ideology, smokers may be left with confusion instead of useful guidance. Public health needs evidence that informs decisions, not evidence selected to protect a narrative. (Published on August 03, 2026bysubstack.com)
